function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have a way to see your actual connection from here, so I can’t tell you what your current download/upload speeds are.  
If you want to find out, you can run a quick speed‑test yourself:

| Option | How to do it |
|--------|--------------|
| **Web browser** | Visit <https://www.speedtest.net> (or any other speed‑test site) and click “Go”. |
| **Command line (Windows)** | 1. Install the free [Speedtest CLI](https://www.speedtest.net/apps/cli). 2. Open PowerShell or CMD and type `speedtest`. |
| **Command line (macOS/Linux)** | 1. Install via Homebrew (`brew install speedtest`) or apt (`sudo apt-get install speedtest`). 2. Run `speedtest` in the terminal. |

If you’d like me to run a command on your machine (e.g., `speedtest`), let me know and I’ll use the `cmd_controller_execute` tool. Otherwise, just try one of the methods above and you’ll get a real‑time measurement of your download and upload speeds.
